overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on either allegation: early release of executive session minutes by the Chair was not barred, and the March 24 executive session minutes substantially complied with detail requirements.

allegations.summary: Chair allegedly released four sets of executive session minutes in response to a records request without a Committee vote authorizing release.
allegations.key_passage: Although the Open Meeting Law allows public bodies to keep executive session discussions confidential for a period of time, the Open Meeting Law does not require that public body members keep topics discussed in executive session confidential prior to the approval and release of the executive session minutes

allegations.summary: Minutes of the March 24 executive session allegedly lacked detail about certain provisions of the Superintendent's contract extension.
allegations.key_passage: After review of the minutes, we find that the Committee substantially complied with the requirement that it provide an accurate and sufficiently detailed summary of the discussion that occurred during the March 24 executive session.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
